title: Hot-route protection: feature flags + staged rollout controls (region allowlist, kill-switch)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds rollout guardrails for hot-route capacity protection: per-region allowlist, kill-switch, and a safe default of "observe-only" until explicitly enabled. No customer-visible behavior change unless flags are enabled.
description: Context: Hot-route capacity protection needs to be rolled out gradually (region-by-region + by tenant cohort) with a fast rollback path during incidents and while we tune thresholds. This PR adds a cohesive rollout control layer used by the gateway/router/policy engine callers to decide whether protections are active, in observe-only mode, or fully enforcing. It also adds a global kill-switch that can be flipped without redeploying to immediately disable enforcement across regions (while still emitting metrics). What’s in this PR: 1) Feature flags: Introduce hot_route_protection_mode with values {disabled, observe_only, enforce}. Disabled = no evaluation and no enforcement (metrics minimal). Observe_only = evaluate policies and emit throttle decisions to logs/metrics but do not block. Enforce = return 429/over-capacity and apply lane admission control. 2) Staged rollout controls: Add per-region allowlist and per-tenant sampling gate (percent rollout) to avoid impacting all traffic at once. Allowlist supports explicit region names (e.g., us-east-1) and a wildcard for internal test envs. 3) Kill-switch: Add control plane override hot_route_protection_kill_switch=true that forces mode=disabled regardless of flag state (cached, polled, and fail-open). Kill-switch state is surfaced to /healthz and exported as a gauge for dashboards/incident bot. 4) Safety defaults + config validation: Default mode is observe_only for production when config exists but rollout has not been explicitly enabled; validation rejects enforce in a region that is not allowlisted. Also adds “config stale” detection to keep behavior stable if control plane fetch fails. 5) Operator UX: Add a minimal admin endpoint in router (/admin/rollout/hot-route-protection) to print the effective rollout decision (mode + region gate + tenant sample) and the last config fetch timestamp, intended for on-call use and for runbook steps. Implementation notes: Rollout decision is calculated via RolloutController in the shared control-plane client package used by gateway + router. The calculation order is: (a) kill-switch (forces disabled), (b) region allowlist gate, (c) tenant sampling, (d) mode flag, (e) stale-config behavior. Stale-config behavior: if last_successful_fetch_age > 10m, we freeze the last known effective decision for 30m and then fall back to disabled (fail-open) to avoid partial enforcement with unknown policy state. This matches the reliability posture discussed in #eng-platform (config fetch failures should not cascade into mass 429s). Example config (control plane): hotRouteProtection: { mode: "observe_only", regionAllowlist: ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"], tenantSamplePercent: 5, killSwitch: false, staleConfigFreezeMinutes: 30, staleConfigDisableAfterMinutes: 40 } Testing: Unit tests cover gating precedence, region parsing, deterministic tenant sampling, stale-config freeze/disable behavior, and kill-switch override. Added an integration-ish test that simulates config updates + fetch failure and asserts decision stability. Rollout plan: Start observe_only at 5% tenant sampling in us-east-1. Verify dashboards: throttling_decision_count (observe-only), lane_admit_decision, config_fetch_age_seconds. After 48h of stable metrics, move to enforce at 1% in us-east-1, then 10%, then add eu-west-1. Kill-switch is the primary rollback lever during incidents (no deploy needed). Follow-ups: a) Wire this controller into the gateway middleware and router enforcement paths (tracked in ENG-4822/ENG-4824). b) Hook kill-switch gauge into incident-bot summary (ENG-??). c) Document operator steps in runbook (Sean/Rafael drafting).
commits: controlplane: add RolloutController for hot-route protection (mode/allowlist/sampling)
router: admin endpoint to inspect effective rollout decision + config age
config: schema + validation for kill-switch, region allowlist, stale-config thresholds
tests: precedence + deterministic tenant sampling + stale-config freeze behavior
observability: export gauges for kill-switch + effective mode by region
changed_areas: gateway (shared lib only): rollout decision wiring hooks (no enforcement yet)
conversation:
Jordan Lee (review): The precedence order looks right. Two asks: (1) Can we make kill-switch force disabled even in observe-only? (2) Please confirm deterministic sampling is stable across restarts and across languages (gateway/router).
Benji Okafor (author): (1) Yes, kill-switch forces disabled regardless of mode (updated tests + comment). (2) Sampling uses tenant_id hashed via xxhash64 with a fixed seed; both gateway and router are Go today and share the same helper. Added a note in code + test that asserts stability.

Rafael Mendes (review): Concern about stale config behavior: freezing for 30m then disabling seems fine, but what happens if we never successfully fetch on startup? We should be explicit that we start in disabled rather than enforce.
Benji Okafor (author): Good catch. Updated logic: on cold start with no last-known decision, effective mode is disabled until first successful fetch; then we can be observe_only/enforce per config. Added test coverage.

Mina Haddad (review): For region allowlist parsing, we should support our internal aliases (use1/euw1) used in some tooling. Otherwise we’ll trip operators.
Benji Okafor (author): Added alias mapping for use1->us-east-1, euw1->eu-west-1, and left the canonical names in the stored/effective decision. Included in admin endpoint output.

Connor O'Brien (review): This is close. Please add a single knob that release eng can flip to force allowlist to only one region without editing the main config doc (less error prone during rollout). Maybe an env override?
Benji Okafor (author): Added optional env override HOT_ROUTE_PROTECTION_REGION_OVERRIDE for emergency narrowing (takes precedence over configured allowlist). It’s logged loudly and exported as a metric label value (boolean only) to avoid cardinality.

Sean Gallagher (review): +1. Please ensure metrics don’t explode: do not label by tenant_id. Also can you add a gauge for config_age_seconds and effective_mode.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed no tenant labels; sampling is internal only. Added config_fetch_age_seconds gauge and effective_mode (as 0/1/2) with region label only.

GitHub Actions (bot): router-integration-tests failed (timeout) on first run.
Benji Okafor (author): Re-ran; looks like a transient runner issue. Second run passed.

Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. This gives us the operational handles we need for game day + initial rollout. Please coordinate with release schedule in #eng-releases once merged.
Benji Okafor (author): Will do; I’ll post the rollout steps and the kill-switch/override knobs.
